newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila rice and corn crops seen weathering El Nino.
newsitem.headline: Manila rice and corn crops seen weathering El Nino.

text.p: Philippines is expected to harvest more rice and corn this year despite threats of a dry spell brought about by the El Nino weather phenomenon, a senior Agriculture Department official said on Tuesday.
"I expect El Nino to have minimal effect on the rice and corn crops," Agriculture Under-secretary Domingo Panganiban said.
"It's been raining in the past several days and rice and corn farmers are busy planting."
Nevertheless, the government is bracing for the worst.
Panganiban said the government is ready to conduct cloud seeding operations in areas that will suffer from minimal rainfall.
The government had dug shallow wells and repaired and opened new irrigation facilities in various areas in the country to irrigate at least 330,000 hectares of farm lands.
Philippine unmilled rice harvest in the first nine months of the year is expected to reach 7.14 million, a meagre 1.05 percent rise over the 1996 level, Panganiban said.

Increased yield per hectare of 1.72 percent is expected to make up for the drop in total harvest area by 0.37 percent. Unmilled rice yield per hectare is seen rising to 2.95 tonnes per hectare from 2.9 due to the distribution of better seed varieties and rehabilitation of irrigation facilities.
But total farm planted to rice is expected to drop to 2.424 million hectares from 2.435 million due to lesser rains in the second half of the year.
Panganiban also expected the country's corn output to increase by 5.49 percent this year from the 4.15 million tonnes in 1996.
Firmer corn prices due to rising domestic demand and the government's distribution of better quality seeds would boost production, he added.
Corn output in the first nine months of the year is projected to increase to 3.458 million tonnes from 3.278 million in the same period last year.

Yield is also forecast to increase to 1.59 tonnes per hectare from 1.54 tonnes while total area harvested is seen growing to 2.17 million hectares from 2.132 million. --Manila newsroom (63 2) 841-8936, Fax 817-6267
